stemMd: An object is placed between a converging lens and its focal point. What kind of image is formed in the thin-lens model?

options.label: E
options.textMd: Real, upright and unchanged in size

explanationMd: Inside the focal length, outgoing rays diverge and their backward extensions meet on the object’s side. This gives a virtual upright magnified image, the principle of a simple magnifying glass. Real-image rules for distant objects do not apply.

distractorRationale.c: That describes a different object-distance regime.
distractorRationale.e: A single converging lens does not give this image for an object inside its focal length.
distractorRationale.a: The image inside this regime is upright and magnified.
distractorRationale.b: A virtual image can be seen by looking through the lens.
